tool.name: DRIMSeq
tool.description: filter transcripts and test for differential transcript usage
tool.command: ln -s '$tx2gene' tx2gene.tsv && ln -s '$samples' samples.txt && #if str($input.type) == "matrix": ln -s '$input.counts_matrix' counts_matrix.tsv && #end if Rscript '$drimseq_script'

configfiles.configfile: #import re #if str($input.type) == "quant": #for $f in $input.quant_files: ${re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]', '_', str($f.element_identifier))} ${f} #end for #end if

suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(DRIMSeq) library(BiocParallel) })
## sample names become column headers and are matched against the sample table, ## so both sides get the same restricted character set clean_names <- function(x) gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", x)
threads <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("GALAXY_SLOTS", "1")) bpparam <- if (threads > 1) MulticoreParam(workers = threads) else SerialParam()
## first column transcript, second column gene; a header line is harmless because ## it never matches a transcript ID tx2gene <- read.delim("tx2gene.tsv", header = FALSE, colClasses = "character", quote = "\"", comment.char = "", na.strings = character(0)) if (ncol(tx2gene) < 2) { stop("The transcript-to-gene table needs two columns: transcript ID, then gene ID.") } tx2gene <- data.frame(tx = tx2gene[[1]], gene_id = tx2gene[[2]]) dup_tx <- duplicated(tx2gene[["tx"]]) if (any(dup_tx)) { message("Transcript-to-gene table lists ", sum(dup_tx), " transcripts more than once; using the first gene for each") tx2gene <- tx2gene[!dup_tx, ] }
#if str($input.type) == "quant": suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tximport)) quant <- read.delim("$quant_table", header = FALSE, colClasses = "character", quote = "", comment.char = "") if (anyDuplicated(quant[[1]])) { stop("Two quantification files have the same sample name: ", paste(unique(quant[[1]][duplicated(quant[[1]])]), collapse = ", ")) } files <- setNames(quant[[2]], quant[[1]]) ## dtuScaledTPM needs a gene for every quantified transcript. Like nf-core/rnasplice, give ## unmapped transcripts (spike-ins, extra contigs) a gene of their own for the import and ## drop them afterwards. quant_tx <- unique(unlist(lapply(files, function(f) { read.delim(f, header = TRUE, colClasses = "character", quote = "", comment.char = "")[[1]] }))) unmapped <- setdiff(quant_tx, tx2gene[["tx"]]) ## the placeholder genes must not share an ID with a real gene, or the unmapped transcript's ## length would enter that gene's median and change its scaled counts prefix <- "unmapped__" while (any(startsWith(tx2gene[["gene_id"]], prefix))) { prefix <- paste0("_", prefix) } txi <- tximport( files, type = "$input.quant_type", txOut = TRUE, countsFromAbundance = "$input.counts_from_abundance", tx2gene = rbind(tx2gene, data.frame(tx = unmapped, gene_id = paste0(prefix, unmapped, recycle0 = TRUE))), dropInfReps = TRUE ) cts <- txi[["counts"]] #else: ## read everything as text so a header that is one field short (R's write.table default) ## or numeric-looking IDs cannot shift or coerce the transcript column raw <- read.delim("counts_matrix.tsv", header = FALSE, colClasses = "character", quote = "\"", comment.char = "", na.strings = character(0), check.names = FALSE) header <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE) raw <- raw[-1, , drop = FALSE] if (ncol(raw) < 2 || nrow(raw) == 0) { stop("The count matrix needs a header line, then a transcript ID column followed by one column per sample.") } if (header[length(header)] == "") { ## a header with no name for the ID column, as R's write.table writes by default header <- c("", header[-length(header)]) } cts <- suppressWarnings(apply(as.matrix(raw[, -1, drop = FALSE]), 2, as.numeric)) cts <- matrix(cts, nrow = nrow(raw), dimnames = list(raw[[1]], header[-1])) if (anyNA(cts)) { stop("The count matrix has empty or non-numeric values outside its first column.") } if (anyDuplicated(rownames(cts))) { stop("The count matrix has duplicated transcript IDs, e.g. ", rownames(cts)[anyDuplicated(rownames(cts))]) } #end if if (any(cts < 0)) { stop("The counts include negative values.") }
colnames(cts) <- clean_names(colnames(cts)) if (anyDuplicated(colnames(cts))) { stop("Sample names are not unique after replacing unusual characters with underscores.") }
#if $samples.is_of_type("csv"): sheet <- read.csv("samples.txt", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = "character", na.strings = character(0), strip.white = TRUE) #else: sheet <- read.delim("samples.txt", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = "character", comment.char = "", na.strings = character(0), strip.white = TRUE) #end if if (!all(c("sample", "condition") %in% colnames(sheet))) { stop("The sample table must have 'sample' and 'condition' column headers.") } sheet <- sheet[, c("sample", "condition")] ## repeated rows for one sample (one per sequencing lane in rnasplice) are fine as long as ## they agree; resolve them on the original names, before cleaning can merge different samples sheet <- sheet[!duplicated(sheet), ] conflicting <- unique(sheet[["sample"]][duplicated(sheet[["sample"]])]) if (length(conflicting) > 0) { stop("The sample table gives different conditions for: ", paste(conflicting, collapse = ", ")) } cleaned <- clean_names(sheet[["sample"]]) collisions <- unique(cleaned[duplicated(cleaned)]) if (length(collisions) > 0) { stop("Different sample names in the sample table become the same after replacing unusual characters with underscores: ", paste(sheet[["sample"]][cleaned %in% collisions], collapse = ", ")) } sheet[["sample"]] <- cleaned
missing <- setdiff(colnames(cts), sheet[["sample"]]) if (length(missing) > 0) { stop("These samples have no row in the sample table: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "), ". The table's sample column must match the dataset names or matrix column headers.") } extra <- setdiff(sheet[["sample"]], colnames(cts)) if (length(extra) > 0) { message("Ignoring sample table rows with no counts: ", paste(extra, collapse = ", ")) } sheet <- sheet[match(colnames(cts), sheet[["sample"]]), ] if (any(sheet[["condition"]] == "")) { stop("These samples have an empty condition: ", paste(sheet[["sample"]][sheet[["condition"]] == ""], collapse = ", ")) } samps <- data.frame(sample_id = sheet[["sample"]], condition = factor(sheet[["condition"]]))
#if str($mode.type) == "test": reference <- "$mode.reference_level" if (nlevels(samps[["condition"]]) != 2) { stop("Testing needs exactly two conditions; the sample table has ", nlevels(samps[["condition"]]), ": ", paste(levels(samps[["condition"]]), collapse = ", ")) } if (!reference %in% levels(samps[["condition"]])) { stop("The reference condition '", reference, "' is not in the sample table's condition column (", paste(levels(samps[["condition"]]), collapse = ", "), ")") } samps[["condition"]] <- relevel(samps[["condition"]], ref = reference) #end if
gene <- tx2gene[["gene_id"]][match(rownames(cts), tx2gene[["tx"]])] if (all(is.na(gene))) { stop("No transcript in the counts is in the transcript-to-gene table, e.g. ", paste(head(rownames(cts), 3), collapse = ", ")) } if (anyNA(gene)) { message("Dropping ", sum(is.na(gene)), " transcripts with no gene in the transcript-to-gene table, e.g. ", paste(head(rownames(cts)[is.na(gene)], 3), collapse = ", ")) } keep <- !is.na(gene) & rowSums(cts) > 0 ## transcripts never seen in any sample carry no information counts <- data.frame(gene_id = gene[keep], feature_id = rownames(cts)[keep], cts[keep, , drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE)
min_samps <- c( min_samps_gene_expr = $filter.min_samps_gene_expr, min_samps_feature_expr = $filter.min_samps_feature_expr, min_samps_feature_prop = $filter.min_samps_feature_prop ) if (any(min_samps > ncol(cts))) { stop("The minimum sample counts (", paste(names(min_samps)[min_samps > ncol(cts)], collapse = ", "), ") cannot exceed the number of samples, ", ncol(cts)) }
d <- dmDSdata(counts = counts, samples = samps) message("Before filtering: ", length(d), " genes, ", nrow(counts(d)), " transcripts") d <- tryCatch( dmFilter( d, min_samps_gene_expr = $filter.min_samps_gene_expr, min_gene_expr = $filter.min_gene_expr, min_samps_feature_expr = $filter.min_samps_feature_expr, min_feature_expr = $filter.min_feature_expr, min_samps_feature_prop = $filter.min_samps_feature_prop, min_feature_prop = $filter.min_feature_prop ), error = function(e) { if (grepl("No genes left after filtering", conditionMessage(e))) { stop("No gene kept two or more transcripts after filtering. Lower the thresholds or check the inputs.", call. = FALSE) } stop(e) } ) message("After filtering: ", length(d), " genes, ", nrow(counts(d)), " transcripts")
write.table(DRIMSeq::samples(d), "samples.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE) write.table(counts(d), "counts.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
#if str($mode.type) == "test": design <- model.matrix(~condition, data = DRIMSeq::samples(d)) coef <- colnames(design)[2] ## dmPrecision estimates its starting value on a random subset of genes set.seed(123) d <- dmPrecision(d, design = design, prec_moderation = "$mode.prec_moderation", BPPARAM = bpparam) d <- dmFit(d, design = design, BPPARAM = bpparam) d <- dmTest(d, coef = coef, BPPARAM = bpparam) write.table(results(d), "gene_results.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE) write.table(results(d, level = "feature"), "transcript_results.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE) write.table(proportions(d), "proportions.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE) #end if
#if str($output_rds) == "true": saveRDS(d, "drimseq.rds") #end if

tool.help:
## What it does
[DRIMSeq](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DRIMSeq) models the transcript counts of each gene with a Dirichlet-multinomial distribution to find differential transcript usage (DTU): changes in the relative proportions of a gene's transcripts between conditions.
This tool runs DRIMSeq's `dmFilter` step, the transcript filter nf-core/rnasplice applies before its DEXSeq-based DTU analysis. It can then run the full DRIMSeq test (`dmPrecision`, `dmFit`, `dmTest`) for one condition with two levels.
The filter keeps a gene only if both of these hold:
- it has at least *minimum gene expression* counts in at least *minimum number of samples where the gene is expressed*; - at least two of its transcripts survive the transcript filters.
A transcript survives if it has at least *minimum transcript expression* counts in enough samples, and makes up at least *minimum transcript proportion* of its gene's counts in enough samples. Transcripts with zero counts in every sample are removed first. The defaults are those of nf-core/rnasplice. The three minimum sample numbers cannot exceed the number of samples.
## Inputs
### Transcript abundances
Either of:
- One Salmon `quant.sf` or kallisto `abundance.tsv` per sample. These are imported with tximport at transcript level. nf-core/rnasplice uses `dtuScaledTPM` counts here. Pick a list collection, e.g. the output of Salmon run over a collection: its element identifiers are the sample names. Plain datasets are named by their history names, which rarely match a sample table. - A transcript count matrix with a header line, transcript IDs in the first column and one column per sample. A header without a name for the ID column (R's `write.table` default) also works.
### Transcript-to-gene table
Transcript ID in column 1, gene ID in column 2. A header line is allowed. Transcripts without a gene are dropped with a message, as nf-core/rnasplice does for spike-ins and other extra sequences in the index.
### Sample table
Tab- or comma-separated, with a header line that contains `sample` and `condition` columns. The nf-core/rnasplice samplesheet works as is.
- Every sample in the counts needs a row with a non-empty condition. - Rows for samples that are not in the counts are ignored. - A sample may appear on several rows (one per lane) only if they all give the same condition. - Characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` are replaced with `_` in sample names, both in the sample table and in the counts, before the two are matched. Two different names that become the same are an error.
## Outputs
Always:
- **Filtered counts**: `gene_id`, `feature_id` and one column per sample, for the transcripts that passed. - **Samples**: `sample_id` and `condition`.
With testing enabled:
- **Gene-level results**: likelihood ratio statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value and adjusted p-value per gene. - **Transcript-level results**: the same per transcript, from DRIMSeq's beta-binomial model. - **Fitted proportions**: the estimated proportion of each transcript in each sample.
On request:
- **R object**: the DRIMSeq object (`dmDSdata` after filtering, `dmDStest` after testing) as an RDS file.
With `dtuScaledTPM` counts, the filtered counts match the table nf-core/rnasplice passes to DEXSeq, except that sample names are cleaned as described above.
## Testing
The reference condition is the baseline. The coefficient tested is the other condition against it, so the sample table must have exactly two conditions. For very small data sets, set precision moderation to *common* or *none*, because the trended estimate needs many genes.
